title: Evaluation of molecular markers to predict the pattern of tumor recurrence and prognosis in pancreatric ductal adenocarcinoma
summary:
Each year, around 15,000 people in Germany are diagnosed with pancreatic carcinoma, which is associated with a very poor prognosis. Surgical therapy is the only potentially curative therapy available today. After the operation chemotherapy is currently recommended to reduce the risk of tumor recurrence. Nevertheless, patients frequently develop local recurrence or distant metastases. 

With the help of modern molecular markers, we aim to predict whether local recurrence or distant metastasis will develop in patients undergoing surgery for pancreatic carcinoma. In the future, these results can be used to optimize the therapy individually for each patient. Patients likely to suffer a local recurrence may benefit from an (additional) local chemoradiotherapy. In this study we also aim to estimate the prognosis of patients suffering from pancreatic cancer with the help of molecular markers.

interventions.name: Construction of a central biobank (tissue samples, blood samples), analysis of molecular markers, correlation with the clinical course of the disease

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspected pancreatic carcinoma, intention to perfom curative surgery
Exclusion criteria:
Patient is inoperable 
No tumor samples can be taken 
No ductal adenocarcinomain the final histology
Overall survival less than 30 days
